starting_state: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. No masks are set, so every step uses the pattern's own note. The sequencer is stopped and the Channel screen is showing.

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The header reads NOTE MASKS CH01 and the value reads X, which means no mask is set, so each step plays its own pattern note.

With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads G3 (MIDI 67). The screen shows the note name, so stop on the readout. This is the channel note mask: all four steps now play G, and their velocities stay as they were.

Hold step 1 at (1,4). The header gains ST01, which means edits now apply to that step only. Turn E3 right until the screen reads C4 (MIDI 72, five detents up from G3). Step 1 has its own note, which overrides the channel default.
Release step 1. The header loses ST01 and the screen returns to the channel default, G3. Playback now starts with C4 (72) and continues G, G, G: a step mask beats the channel mask.
Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads D4 (MIDI 74) and release the step. Steps 1 and 2 each have their own note (C4, D4), and steps 3 and 4 still play the channel note G.
Hold step 1 and press K2, then release the step. Step 1's mask is cleared, so it plays G3 again from the channel default, and step 2 still plays D4.
With no step held, hold K1 and press K2. Every step exception is cleared at once and the channel default stays: the screen still reads G3 and all four steps play G again.
